title: The Shapes and Colors of a Near-Death Experience - Nautilus
gist: Researcher France Lerner had 50 near-death-experience reporters reconstruct their experiences with geometric drawings and colors, finding four spatial types — cones, broad arches, gentle curves and egg-like interiors — with cones resembling the classic tunnel of light.

insights.claim: Some studies estimate that 4 to 8 percent of the global population, and up to 23 percent of cardiac arrest survivors, have had a near-death experience.
insights.so_what: Prevalence data; no direct market angle.
insights.quote: between four and eight percent of the global population has had one, as have up to 23 percent of cardiac arrest survivors
insights.speaker: Kristen French

insights.claim: In a study by neurophenomenology researcher France Lerner and colleagues, 50 people who reported near-death experiences reconstructed them as geometric drawings and described four types of spaces: cones, broad arches, gentle curves and egg-interior-like spaces.
insights.so_what: Novel phenomenological methodology for studying consciousness.
insights.quote: The participants reported entering four types of spaces: cones, broad arches, gentle curves, and spaces resembling the inside of an egg.
insights.speaker: Kristen French

insights.claim: The researchers note the cone shapes reported by near-death experiencers resemble the tunnels ending in bright lights characteristic of NDE stories.
insights.so_what: Suggests common perceptual structure behind NDE narratives.
insights.speaker: Kristen French
